newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: QNI/Gencor link highlights Australian nickel boom.
newsitem.headline: QNI/Gencor link highlights Australian nickel boom.

text.p: The announcement on Wednesday of a merger of the nickel operations of South Africa's Gencor Ltd and Australia's QNI Ltd has given another boost to a nickel boom in Australia, more well known for its gold plays.
QNI sources most of its ore for processing from the French territory of New Caledonia and some from Indonesia, given the location of its Yabulu refinery on Australia's Eastern seaboard.
But prospectors 3,000 km west on the other side of the country say there's plenty of nickel to find in Australia.

Australian nickel mine production should rise 15 percent in the fiscal year ending June 30, 1998, following an estimated increase of 8.5 percent in the last 12 months, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) says.
Refined production will grow 7.5 percent to 72,000 tonnes next year after soaring 17 percent in the previous year, the government commodities forecaster said this week.

The potential rewards from nickel have turned the attention of the otherwise gold-obsessed mining town of Kalgoorlie to nickel. WMC Ltd, the world's fourth largest producer, has long mined the nickel-rich Kambalda lode near the the town.
Next year the A$900 million Murrin Murrin nickel project is scheduled to start up, contributing some 45,000 tonnes of nickel and 3,000 tonnes of cobalt to the world pool.
By that time, partners Outokumpu Oy of Finland and Australia-based Mining Project Investors Pty will have fully commissioned the Silver Swan mine, also near Kalgoorlie.

Silver Swan's forecast production of about 29,000 tonnes of mine concentrate a year has been earmarked for Outokumpu's Harjavalta smelter, which already is getting supplies from the Forrestania nickel mine in Western Australia.

Broker J B Were estimates that from next year, production from three new Australian projects on the boards, Centaur Mining and Exploration Ltd's Cawse mine, the Bulong project being funded by Resolute Ltd, and Silver Swan will sport combined capacity to make 30,000 tonnes of refined metal.
Meanwhile, Canada's Lionore Mining International Ltd is bringing on the Maggie Hays project via recently acquired Forrestania Gold NL and in partnership with Gencor.
With consumption forecasts for annual growth of around five percent for nickel, used widely in stainless steelmaking, there is little concern the market will bottom out soon.
Demand for the metal is expected continue to outpace production, at least until the giant Voisey's Bay mine in Labrador, Canada is opened.
The giant find is geared to contribute about 16 percent of world output when it comes on stream in about three years.
"We're fairly confident nickel prices will be reasonable over the next four to five years," Stephen Dennis, manager of the Murrin Murrin project, told Reuters.
QNI said earlier it would merge operations with Gencor with the South African miner holding up to 56 percent of QNI.
The deal effectively sews up about eight percent of the world nickel market.
